issues.legal_issue: A person whose property has vested in an administrator with the powers to possess, manage, lease, sell, and collect income from it, while the person retains only a restricted beneficial interest, is not the owner of that property for purposes of taxation of income from property.
material_facts: The assessee had an interest in a hotel that was declared evacuee property and vested in a custodian under the governing ordinance.
The custodian could take possession of the property, collect its income, manage it, and in specified circumstances alienate or demolish it.
The assessee could not take possession of, lease, mortgage, sell, or collect income from the property without the custodian’s consent, and could not appropriate the property’s proceeds.
The assessee claimed deductions for interest relating to the property, but reported its annual letting value as nil.
The dispute arose in assessments of income from property under the Income-tax Act, 1922.
issues.conclusion: The assessee was not the owner of the property for purposes of section 9 of the Income-tax Act, 1922, during the relevant assessment years; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9 of the Income-tax Act, 1922 taxes income from property, rather than a person’s interest in property. For that purpose, the owner is the person who can exercise the rights of ownership in their own right. Under sections 6, 9, 11, 12, 14, 16, 19, 20 and 22 of the Pakistan (Administration of Evacuee Property) Ordinance, 1949, the custodian’s powers over vested evacuee property were those of its legal owner, although the evacuee retained a residual beneficial interest. The Court applied The Official Assignee for Bengal (Estate of Jnanendra Nath Pramanik), Commissioner of Inland Revenue v. Fleming, and Sir Currimbhoy Ibrahim Baronetcy Trust v. Commissioner of Income-tax, and distinguished Amar Singh v. Custodian, Evacuee Property, Punjab. It considered, but found no support for the assessee’s position in, P.C. Lal Choudhary v. Commissioner of Income-tax and Nawab Bahadur of Murshidabad v. Commissioner of Income-tax.

rule.if: property_income_tax_assessment and property_vested_in_administrator and administrator_exercises_ownership_powers and former_owner_cannot_control_or_receive_property_income

predicates.property_income_tax_assessment: The proceeding concerns taxation of income from property.
predicates.property_vested_in_administrator: The property vested in an administrator under a legal arrangement for its administration.
predicates.administrator_exercises_ownership_powers: The administrator could possess, manage, dispose of, or collect income from the property in the administrator’s own capacity.
predicates.former_owner_cannot_control_or_receive_p: The former owner could not control the property or receive its income without the administrator’s consent.

issues.definition: When a property-income tax assessment concerns property vested in an administrator who exercises ownership powers while the former owner cannot control the property or receive its income, the former owner is not treated as its owner for that tax.
